AAC-001.q: A parent sells goods to its subsidiary: cost 800, price 1,000 (VND million). At year-end the subsidiary still holds 40% of these goods. What unrealised profit must be eliminated on consolidation (VND million)?
AAC-001.e: Intra-group profit = 1,000 − 800 = 200; portion still in inventory = 200 × 40% = 80 million VND.
AAC-001.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10 (eliminating unrealised profit).
Working: Intra-group profit = 1,000 − 800 = 200 (20% of price). 40% remains in the subsidiary's stock → unrealised profit = 200 × 40% = 80 million VND.
Note: The 60% sold outside the group is realised and not eliminated.

AAC-002.q: A parent sells goods to its subsidiary: cost 800, price 1,000 (VND million); at year-end the subsidiary still holds 40% (unrealised profit 80). The consolidation elimination entry (ignoring tax) is:
AAC-002.e: Eliminate all intra-group revenue and cost of sales and reduce inventory by the unrealised profit.
o: Dr Revenue 1,000 / Cr Cost of sales 920 / Cr Inventory 80
Dr Cost of sales 1,000 / Cr Revenue 1,000
Dr Inventory 80 / Cr Revenue 80
No elimination needed as they are separate legal entities
AAC-002.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10; Circular 202/2014/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Entry: Dr Revenue 1,000 (eliminating all intra-group sales) / Cr COGS 920 (1,000 − 80) / Cr Inventory 80. Check: group cost of the 60% sold externally = 480 (cost), the subsidiary recorded 600 → minus 120; the parent's COGS 800 → eliminated; total COGS reduction 920.
Distractors: B only swaps revenue and cost, missing profit in stock; C is reversed; D breaches the single-entity principle.

AAC-003.q: Unrealised intra-group profit of VND 80 million is eliminated from inventory; CIT rate 20%. What deferred tax asset is recognised on consolidation (VND million)?
AAC-003.e: Consolidated carrying amount is 80 below the tax base → deductible temporary difference; DTA = 80 × 20% = 16 million VND.
AAC-003.x:
Basis: VAS 17; VAS 25; IAS 12.
Working: In the consolidated FS, stock at group cost is 80 below its tax base (the subsidiary's purchase price) → a deductible temporary difference → deferred tax asset = 80 × 20% = 16 million VND (Dr 243 / Cr 8212).
Note: Use the tax rate of the entity holding the goods (the subsidiary).

AAC-004.q: When a non-wholly-owned subsidiary sells to its parent (upstream), the eliminated unrealised profit is allocated between parent shareholders and non-controlling interests.
AAC-004.e: True. The profit arose in the subsidiary, so it affects the NCI share of profit.
AAC-004.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Analysis: True. In upstream sales the profit sits in the subsidiary's earnings, which are shared between the parent and NCI → the elimination is split by ownership (AAC-005, AAC-018). In downstream sales (parent to subsidiary) the whole elimination hits the parent's profit.

AAC-005.q: An 80%-owned subsidiary sells to its parent; unrealised profit at year-end is VND 50 million. How much of the elimination is allocated to NCI (VND million)?
AAC-005.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Working: NCI share of the elimination = 50 × (1 − 80%) = 50 × 20% = 10 million VND; the parent bears 40 million (ignoring tax).

AAC-006.q: 80% of company B is acquired for VND 600 billion; fair value of B's identifiable net assets is 650 billion; NCI measured at its proportionate share. What is goodwill (VND billion)?
AAC-006.x:
Basis: VAS 11; IFRS 3.
Working: NCI = 20% × 650 = 130 (AAC-007). Goodwill = consideration 600 + NCI 130 − net assets 650 = 80 billion VND. Alternatively: 600 − 80% × 650 = 600 − 520 = 80.

AAC-007.q: 80% of company B is acquired for VND 600 billion; fair value of B's identifiable net assets is 650 billion; NCI measured at its proportionate share. What is NCI at the acquisition date (VND billion)?
AAC-007.x:
Basis: VAS 11; IFRS 3 (NCI at proportionate net assets – IFR-130).
Working: NCI at acquisition = 20% × 650 = 130 billion VND.
Note: Measuring NCI at fair value (IFRS only) makes both NCI and goodwill larger.

AAC-008.q: Under Vietnamese consolidation rules, goodwill of VND 80 billion is amortised straight-line over at most 10 years. Using 10 years, what is the annual charge (VND billion)?
AAC-008.e: 80 / 10 = 8 billion VND per year; under IFRS goodwill is not amortised but tested annually for impairment.
AAC-008.x:
Basis: Circular 202/2014/TT-BTC (Vietnamese consolidation rules); IFRS 3; IAS 36.
Working: Straight-line over 10 years: 80 / 10 = 8 billion VND a year.
Note: Under IFRS goodwill isn't amortised but tested annually (IFR-012, IFR-113) – IFRS consolidated profit is 8 billion a year higher absent impairment.

AAC-009.q: A parent lends VND 50 billion to its subsidiary at 8% per year. On consolidation the group must:
AAC-009.e: The group is presented as a single economic entity; intra-group balances and transactions are fully eliminated.
o: Eliminate the loan receivable/payable and the intra-group interest income/expense
Eliminate only the receivable
Keep everything as there is a loan contract
Reclassify the loan to equity
AAC-009.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Analysis: The group is one economic entity: an internal loan isn't an external asset or liability → eliminate the 50 billion receivable–payable pair and the 4 billion a year interest income–expense pair (50 × 8%).
Distractors: B eliminates only half; C breaches the entity concept; D has no basis.
Note: Separate FS and tax still record it (related-party interest faces the 30% of EBITDA cap).

AAC-010.q: An 80%-owned subsidiary pays total dividends of VND 100 billion. How much dividend income must be eliminated on consolidation (VND billion)?
AAC-010.e: The parent's 80 billion dividend income is eliminated; the 20 billion paid to NCI reduces non-controlling interests.
AAC-010.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Working: The parent's share 80% × 100 = 80 billion is an internal transfer → eliminate the dividend income. The 20 billion paid to NCI is with outsiders → it reduces NCI (and is a financing cash flow in the consolidated cash flow statement).

AAC-011.q: When a parent sells PP&E to its subsidiary at a gain, the gain is eliminated on consolidation and the extra depreciation from the inflated carrying amount is adjusted over the remaining useful life.
AAC-011.e: True. Consolidated assets must reflect the group's original cost.
AAC-011.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Analysis: True. Profit on an intra-group asset sale is unrealised for the group → eliminated, restating the asset to group cost. The subsidiary depreciates the inflated amount → the excess depreciation is reversed each year over the remaining life (AAC-012) – the internal profit is 'realised' gradually through depreciation.

AAC-012.q: At the start of the year a parent sells equipment to its subsidiary for VND 500 million; carrying amount 400 million; remaining life 5 years. By how much is depreciation reduced on consolidation in year 1 (VND million)?
AAC-012.e: The 100 intra-group gain spreads over 5 years → depreciation is inflated by 20 million per year and must be reversed.
AAC-012.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Working: Internal profit = 500 − 400 = 100 million. Subsidiary depreciation = 500/5 = 100; at group cost = 400/5 = 80 → reduce by 20 million a year (100/5).
Note: Year 1: eliminate 100 profit, cut depreciation 20 → consolidated profit falls net 80; unrealised profit left at year-end 80.

AAC-013.q: When a parent loses control of a subsidiary but retains 30%, under IFRS 10 the parent:
AAC-013.e: Loss of control is a significant economic event; the retained interest is remeasured at fair value.
o: Derecognises the assets, liabilities and NCI; measures the retained interest at fair value; recognises the gain/loss in profit or loss
Continues consolidating 30%
Keeps the retained interest at old book value with no gain/loss
Takes the entire difference to equity
AAC-013.x:
Basis: IFRS 10, paragraph 25 and B97–B99.
Analysis: On loss of control: derecognise the former subsidiary's assets, liabilities (including goodwill) and NCI; recognise consideration and the 30% retained at fair value (becoming an associate under IAS 28); take the difference to profit or loss; reclassify related OCI or move it to retained earnings.
Distractors: B, C and D breach IFRS 10.

AAC-014.q: Under IFRS 10, a parent buying more shares in a subsidiary it already controls (from 70% to 90%) is an equity transaction with no gain/loss or new goodwill.
AAC-014.e: True. The difference between the price paid and the reduction in NCI goes directly to equity.
AAC-014.x:
Basis: IFRS 10, paragraph 23.
Analysis: True. Ownership changes without losing control are transactions between owners (parent and NCI) → equity transactions: adjust NCI and take the difference between consideration and the NCI reduction directly to the parent's equity; no gain or loss, no remeasurement, no new goodwill.

AAC-015.q: An investor holding 30% of an associate sells goods to it at a profit of VND 100 million; at year-end the associate has not resold them. How much unrealised profit must the investor eliminate (VND million)?
AAC-015.e: For associates only the investor's share is eliminated: 100 × 30% = 30 million VND.
AAC-015.x:
Basis: VAS 07; IAS 28.
Working: For associates (not consolidated line by line), only the investor's share of unrealised profit is eliminated: 100 × 30% = 30 million VND (reducing share of profit or the investment).
Note: Unlike subsidiaries (AAC-001) – fully eliminated.

AAC-016.q: A subsidiary's FS used for consolidation have a different reporting date from the parent. The maximum difference usually allowed (adjusting for significant transactions) is:
AAC-016.e: VAS 25 and IFRS 10 allow up to 3 months, with adjustments for significant transactions and events in between.
o: No more than 3 months
No more than 6 months
No more than 12 months
No limit
AAC-016.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10 (B92–B93).
Analysis: Subsidiaries should report at the parent's date; if not, the gap may not exceed 3 months and significant transactions or events in between must be adjusted; period lengths and gaps must be consistent over time.
Distractors: B, C and D exceed the limit.

AAC-017.q: Select ALL correct requirements when preparing consolidated FS:
AAC-017.e: Subsidiaries in different industries must still be consolidated if controlled.
o: Apply uniform accounting policies across the group
Eliminate the parent's investment against the subsidiary's corresponding equity
Eliminate all intra-group balances
Present NCI within equity
Exclude subsidiaries in different industries from consolidation
AAC-017.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Analysis: Requirements: (A) uniform accounting policies (adjusting subsidiaries that differ); (B) eliminating the investment against the related equity; (C) eliminating all intra-group balances and transactions (AAC-009); (D) presenting NCI within equity, separate from the parent's share.
Distractors: (E) Subsidiaries in different businesses must still be consolidated if controlled – exclusion for dissimilar activities isn't allowed.

AAC-018.q: A subsidiary's profit after tax is VND 200 billion; NCI holds 25%; unrealised upstream profit is 40 billion (ignore tax). What profit is attributed to NCI (VND billion)?
AAC-018.x:
Basis: VAS 25; IFRS 10.
Working: Subsidiary profit after eliminating upstream profit = 200 − 40 = 160 billion. NCI share = 25% × 160 = 40 billion VND (AAC-004).

AAC-019.q: An annual distributor contract: price VND 100 thousand per unit, retrospective 5% rebate on all volume if purchases exceed 8,000 units/year; the entity judges this highly probable (10,000 expected). Q1 sales are 3,000 units. What is Q1 revenue (VND million)?
AAC-019.e: Recognise at the expected net price: 3,000 × 95 thousand = 285 million VND; 15 million is a refund liability.
AAC-019.x:
Basis: VAS 14; IFRS 15 (variable consideration – volume rebates).
Working: Reaching the threshold is near-certain → expected price = 100 × 95% = 95 thousand per unit. Q1 revenue = 3,000 × 95 = 285 million; 3,000 × 5 = 15 million is a refund liability (rebate to pay).
Note: If the threshold were uncertain, apply the constraint (IFR-049), recognise at 100 and adjust when the assessment changes.

AAC-020.q: A machine is sold with payment of VND 1,210 million due in exactly 2 years; the equivalent cash price uses a 10% market rate. What sales revenue is recognised on delivery (VND million)?
AAC-020.e: 1,210 / 1.1² = 1,000 million VND; 210 million is finance income recognised over 2 years.
AAC-020.x:
Basis: VAS 14; IFRS 15 (significant financing component – IFR-057).
Working: Sales revenue = PV = 1,210 / 1.1² = 1,000 million VND at delivery. The 210 million difference is finance income recognised at the effective rate: year 1 = 100, year 2 = 110.

AAC-021.q: Which indicator suggests an entity is a principal rather than an agent in a sale?
AAC-021.e: A principal controls the goods/services before transfer and records gross revenue.
o: It is primarily responsible for fulfilment, bears inventory risk and sets the price
It earns only a fixed commission per transaction
It never controls the goods
The supplier bears all return risk
AAC-021.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, Appendix B (B34–B38).
Analysis: Principal indicators (control before transfer): primary responsibility for fulfilment; inventory risk before or after transfer; discretion over price → gross revenue.
Distractors: B, C and D indicate an agent (net revenue – IFR-053).

AAC-022.q: The transaction price allocated to loyalty points is based on the points' relative standalone selling price, not on the entity's cost of redemption.
AAC-022.e: True under IFRS 15; redemption cost is at most an input to estimating standalone price.
AAC-022.x:
Basis: IFRS 15 (allocation by relative standalone selling price).
Analysis: True. Loyalty points are a material right → a separate performance obligation; the price is allocated by the points' relative standalone selling price (value to the customer on redemption, adjusted for expected redemption), not the entity's cost of redeeming them (IFR-056). Cost is only an input when no observable price exists (cost-plus approach).

AAC-023.q: A fixed-price construction contract of VND 1,000 billion now has total expected costs of 1,100 billion. What loss must be recognised immediately (VND billion)?
AAC-023.e: When expected costs exceed contract revenue, the expected loss is recognised immediately (onerous contract).
AAC-023.x:
Basis: VAS 15; IAS 37 (onerous contracts).
Working: Expected loss = total expected cost 1,100 − contract revenue 1,000 = 100 billion VND, expensed immediately once identified, regardless of progress – not spread by stage of completion.

AAC-024.q: A customer asks the entity to hold goods already purchased (bill-and-hold) because its warehouse isn't ready. Which condition is required to recognise revenue before delivery?
AAC-024.e: Missing any condition means control hasn't passed; invoicing is not a basis.
o: A substantive reason, goods identified separately as the customer's, ready for delivery and unavailable to other customers
The customer paid a 10% deposit
The entity issued an invoice
Production is complete
AAC-024.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, B79–B82 (IFR-058).
Analysis: Beyond general control indicators, all four are needed: a substantive reason (usually the customer's request); goods separately identified as the customer's; ready for delivery; unusable for or transferable to others.
Distractors: B, C and D don't prove control has passed – invoicing isn't a basis for revenue.

AAC-025.q: Goods shipped on terms where the seller is responsible until the buyer's warehouse, dispatched 30/12 but received 03/01 next year, generate revenue in the next year.
AAC-025.e: True. Control passes on receipt at the customer's warehouse; this is a key cut-off test point.
AAC-025.x:
Basis: VAS 14; IFRS 15; Incoterms (delivery terms).
Analysis: True. With the seller responsible up to the buyer's warehouse → risk and control pass on receipt on 03/01 → revenue belongs to next year though shipped on 30/12 (at year-end the goods are still the seller's stock in transit). A key cut-off check (ICR-141, VSA-127).

AAC-026.q: A retail chain sells VND 1,000 million of gift cards; 10% is expected never to be used (breakage). Customers redeem 450 million during the year. What revenue is recognised in the year (VND million)?
AAC-026.e: Breakage of 100 is recognised in proportion to redemptions: 100 × 450/900 = 50; revenue = 450 + 50 = 500 million VND.
AAC-026.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, B44–B47 (customers' unexercised rights – breakage).
Working: Expected breakage = 10% × 1,000 = 100; expected redemptions = 900. Redeemed 450 = 50% → recognise breakage proportionately 100 × 450/900 = 50. Revenue for the year = 450 + 50 = 500 million VND; 500 million remains a contract liability.

AAC-027.q: An entity sells phones with an optional 2-year extended warranty that customers can buy separately. The extended warranty is accounted for:
AAC-027.e: Service-type warranties (separately purchasable) are separate performance obligations.
o: As a separate performance obligation, with revenue over 2 years
As a warranty provision under IAS 37
As revenue at the point of sale
As a reduction of cost of sales
AAC-027.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, B28–B33 (IFR-059, IFR-060).
Analysis: A separately purchasable 2-year extended warranty is service-type → a separate performance obligation; allocate the price and recognise revenue over the 2 years.
Distractors: B is for assurance-type warranties; C is too early; D misreads it.

AAC-028.q: Goods on consignment are not recognised as revenue when delivered to the consignee.
AAC-028.e: True. Revenue arises when the consignee sells to the end customer (control transfers).
AAC-028.x:
Basis: VAS 14; IFRS 15 (consignment – B77–B78).
Analysis: True. On delivery to the agent the business still controls the goods (it can recall or redirect them; the agent has no unconditional payment duty) → no revenue yet; they become goods on consignment. Revenue arises when the agent sells to the end customer (IFR-159).

AAC-029.q: Sales with a right of return: revenue 2,000, cost 1,200 (VND million); 5% expected to be returned. What 'right to recover goods' asset is recognised (VND million, assuming no impairment of returns)?
AAC-029.e: Revenue 1,900; refund liability 100; right-to-recover asset = 1,200 × 5% = 60 million VND.
AAC-029.x:
Basis: IFRS 15 (right of return – IFR-061).
Working: Revenue = 2,000 × 95% = 1,900; refund liability = 100. Right-to-recover asset = cost of expected returns = 1,200 × 5% = 60 million VND; COGS recognised = 1,200 − 60 = 1,140.

AAC-030.q: An entity licenses its brand to franchisees; the brand's value depends heavily on the licensor's ongoing promotion. Licence fee revenue is recognised:
AAC-030.e: When the licensor continues to affect the IP, the customer gets a right to access → revenue over time.
o: Over time (right to access)
At a point in time (right to use)
When cash is received
When the contract expires
AAC-030.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, B58–B63 (licences of intellectual property).
Analysis: The licensor's ongoing activities significantly affect the brand (continuous promotion), directly exposing the customer → a right to access → revenue over time. IP with standalone functionality (software, finished films) is a right to use, recognised at a point in time.
Distractors: B, C and D don't fit the model.

AAC-031.q: Costs to fulfil a contract (e.g., setting up a system for a customer) are capitalised if directly related, they generate resources used to satisfy obligations and are expected to be recovered.
AAC-031.e: True under IFRS 15; otherwise they are expensed immediately.
AAC-031.x:
Basis: IFRS 15, paragraphs 95–98 (costs to fulfil a contract).
Analysis: True. Fulfilment costs (not covered by other standards like IAS 2 or IAS 16) are capitalised when: directly related to the contract; generating or enhancing resources used to satisfy future obligations; and expected to be recovered. They're amortised with the service pattern; otherwise expensed.

AAC-032.q: A bundle priced at VND 900 million includes A (standalone price 600) and B (standalone price 400). What revenue is allocated to A (VND million)?
AAC-032.e: The discount is allocated pro rata to standalone prices: 900 × 600/1,000 = 540 million VND.
AAC-032.x:
Basis: IFRS 15.
Working: Standalone total = 600 + 400 = 1,000; bundle discount 100. A = 900 × 600/1,000 = 540; B = 900 × 400/1,000 = 360 million VND.

AAC-033.q: Machinery has a book carrying amount of VND 700 million and a tax written-down value of 500 million (faster tax depreciation). Tax rate 20%. What deferred tax liability arises (VND million)?
AAC-033.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12.
Working: Taxable temporary difference = carrying amount 700 − tax base 500 = 200 → deferred tax liability = 200 × 20% = 40 million VND (Dr 8212 / Cr 347).

AAC-034.q: A warranty provision of VND 300 million is booked but is tax-deductible only when paid. Tax rate 20%. What deferred tax asset arises (VND million)?
AAC-034.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12; CIT Law (warranty provisions deductible only when paid – per the question's source).
Working: The provision's carrying amount is 300 with a tax base of 0 → a deductible temporary difference of 300 → deferred tax asset = 300 × 20% = 60 million VND (Dr 243 / Cr 8212), provided future taxable profit is probable.

AAC-035.q: A deferred tax asset for unused tax losses is recognised when:
AAC-035.e: A history of recent losses is strong contrary evidence; other convincing evidence is required.
o: It is probable that sufficient future taxable profit will be available to use the losses
Management has an optimistic business plan
Always in full
Never
AAC-035.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12 (IFR-138).
Analysis: Recognise only to the extent that sufficient future taxable profit is probable to use the losses within the carry-forward period (5 years in Vietnam). A record of continuing losses is strong contrary evidence.
Distractors: B – an optimistic plan isn't enough evidence; C and D are extremes.

AAC-036.q: The deferred tax liability is VND 40 million at the start and 55 million at year-end (all movements through profit or loss). What is the deferred tax expense for the year (VND million)?
AAC-036.e: 55 − 40 = 15 million VND (debit deferred income tax expense).
AAC-036.x:
Basis: VAS 17.
Working: Deferred tax expense = change in the deferred tax liability = 55 − 40 = 15 million VND (Dr 8212 / Cr 347).

AAC-037.q: Non-deductible administrative fines are permanent differences and create no deferred tax.
AAC-037.e: True. Only temporary differences give rise to deferred tax.
AAC-037.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12; CIT Law (administrative fines are non-deductible).
Analysis: True. Fines are never tax-deductible → a permanent difference that never reverses → no deferred tax; they only push the effective rate above the statutory rate (AAC-039).

AAC-038.q: Accounting profit before tax VND 1,000 million; non-deductible fines 50 million; tax depreciation exceeds book depreciation by 100 million (new taxable temporary difference). Tax 20%. What is total income tax expense (current + deferred) (VND million)?
AAC-038.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12.
Working: Taxable income = 1,000 + 50 (fine, permanent) − 100 (excess tax depreciation, temporary) = 950 → current tax = 950 × 20% = 190. Deferred tax = 100 × 20% = 20. Total tax expense = 210 million VND.
Check: (1,000 + 50) × 20% = 210 – temporary differences shift timing, not the total.

AAC-039.q: Accounting profit before tax VND 1,000 million; non-deductible fines 50 million; tax depreciation exceeds book depreciation by 100 million (new temporary difference). Tax 20% → total income tax expense (current + deferred) 210 million. What is the effective tax rate (total tax / accounting PBT) (%)?
AAC-039.e: 210 / 1,000 = 21%: above 20% because of non-deductible fines (a permanent difference).
AAC-039.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12 (effective tax rate reconciliation).
Working: Effective rate = 210 / 1,000 = 21%. Reconciliation: 20% statutory + non-deductible fine 50 × 20% / 1,000 = 1% = 21%.

AAC-040.q: Deferred tax on a PP&E revaluation surplus recognised in OCI is recognised:
AAC-040.e: Deferred tax follows the underlying item.
o: In the same place as the underlying item (OCI/equity)
In profit or loss
Not at all
In finance income
AAC-040.x:
Basis: IAS 12, paragraph 61A.
Analysis: Deferred tax on items recognised outside profit or loss follows the item: a revaluation surplus in OCI → its deferred tax liability also goes to OCI (reducing the net surplus – IFR-106).
Distractors: B, C and D breach the principle.

AAC-041.q: Deferred tax assets and liabilities may be offset only if there is a legally enforceable right and they relate to taxes levied by the same tax authority.
AAC-041.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12, paragraph 74.
Analysis: True. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are offset only if there's a legal right to offset current tax and they relate to the same taxation authority (the same taxpayer, or entities intending net settlement). In consolidated FS, different subsidiaries' deferred taxes usually can't be netted.

AAC-042.q: Match each item with its account under the enterprise accounting regime:
AAC-042.e: Current income tax expense is recorded in account 8211.
AAC-042.x:
Basis: Circular 99/2025/TT-BTC.
Analysis: Deferred tax assets – account 243; deferred tax liabilities – account 347; deferred CIT expense – account 8212 (current tax – 8211; global minimum top-up tax – 82112 per ACC-021).

AAC-043.q: An entity has tax losses carried forward of VND 500 million; reliable forecasts show only 60% will probably be used within the carry-forward period. Tax 20%. What DTA is recognised (VND million)?
AAC-043.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12.
Working: Losses expected to be used = 500 × 60% = 300 million → deferred tax asset = 300 × 20% = 60 million VND; the other 200 million is unrecognised (disclosed).

AAC-044.q: Deferred tax assets and liabilities are not discounted.
AAC-044.x:
Basis: VAS 17; IAS 12, paragraph 53.
Analysis: True. Deferred tax assets and liabilities aren't discounted – scheduling the reversal of every temporary difference is usually impractical or complex; banning discounting keeps entities comparable.

AAC-045.q: 1,000 units are sold with warranty: 90% expected defect-free, 8% minor defects (VND 0.1 million each), 2% major (1 million each). What is the expected-value warranty provision (VND million)?
AAC-045.x:
Basis: VAS 18; IAS 37 (expected value for large populations).
Working: Minor defects 8% × 1,000 = 80 units × 0.1 = 8 million; major 2% × 1,000 = 20 units × 1 = 20 million. Provision = 8 + 20 = 28 million VND.

AAC-046.q: For a single obligation (e.g., one lawsuit), a provision is usually measured at:
AAC-046.e: Expected value is used for large populations of similar obligations (such as warranties).
o: The most likely outcome, considering other outcomes
The expected value of a large population
The lowest possible amount
The amount claimed by the plaintiff
AAC-046.x:
Basis: VAS 18; IAS 37, paragraph 40.
Analysis: A single obligation (one lawsuit) is measured at the most likely outcome, considering others – if most other outcomes are higher, the provision exceeds the most likely amount.
Distractors: B is for large populations (AAC-045); C and D aren't the best estimate.

AAC-047.q: A contingent liability whose outflow is remote need not be disclosed.
AAC-047.e: True. Contingent liabilities are disclosed unless the possibility of outflow is remote.
AAC-047.x:
Basis: VAS 18; IAS 37 (IFR-141).
Analysis: True. Contingent liabilities are disclosed (nature, estimated effect, uncertainties) unless the outflow is remote – then no disclosure is needed, avoiding cluttering the FS with unhelpful information.

AAC-048.q: Slow-moving work in progress costs VND 500 million; estimated selling price 520 million; estimated cost to complete 60 million; selling costs 20 million. What write-down is required (VND million)?
AAC-048.x:
Basis: VAS 02; IAS 2.
Working: NRV = price 520 − completion 60 − selling 20 = 440. Write-down = cost 500 − 440 = 60 million VND.
Note: Omitting completion costs gives NRV 500 – no write-down, which is wrong.

AAC-049.q: Receivables ECL matrix: current 2,000 (0.5%); 31–60 days 400 (4%); 61–90 days 200 (15%); over 90 days 100 (60%) – VND million. What is the ECL allowance (VND million)?
AAC-049.x:
Basis: IFRS 9 (provision matrix – IFR-090).
Working: 2,000 × 0.5% = 10; 400 × 4% = 16; 200 × 15% = 30; 100 × 60% = 60. Total = 10 + 16 + 30 + 60 = 116 million VND.
Note: Under Circular 48/2019 only debts 6+ months overdue are provided for – a much lower VAS allowance.

AAC-050.q: Changing the warranty provision rate due to new defect-rate data is:
AAC-050.e: Estimates change with new information; effects go to current and future periods.
o: A change in accounting estimate – applied prospectively
A change in accounting policy – applied retrospectively
A prior-period error
Not recognised
AAC-050.x:
Basis: VAS 29; IAS 8.
Analysis: The warranty provision rate is an estimate; revising it with new defect data is a change in estimate → prospective, affecting current and future periods.
Distractors: B – the policy (recognition and measurement basis) is unchanged; C – it isn't an error if the earlier estimate reasonably used available information; D is wrong.

AAC-051.q: PP&E cost VND 1,200 million, original life 10 years (straight-line, no residual). After 4 years the remaining life is revised to only 4 years. What is year-5 depreciation (VND million)?
AAC-051.e: Carrying amount after 4 years = 1,200 − 4 × 120 = 720; new depreciation = 720 / 4 = 180 million VND per year.
AAC-051.x:
Basis: VAS 03; VAS 29 (change in estimate – prospective).
Working: Old depreciation = 1,200 / 10 = 120 a year; after 4 years the carrying amount = 1,200 − 480 = 720. With 4 years left → year-5 depreciation = 720 / 4 = 180 million VND; the past 4 years aren't restated (ACC-080, IFR-032).

AAC-052.q: A site restoration obligation of VND 1,000 million is payable in 10 years; discount rate 8% per year. What is the initial provision (present value) (VND million, 2 decimals)?
AAC-052.e: 1,000 / 1.08¹⁰ = 1,000 / 2.1589 ≈ 463.19 million VND; the asset's cost increases by the same amount.
AAC-052.x:
Basis: IAS 37; IAS 16 (dismantling and restoration costs – paragraph 16(c)).
Working: Initial provision = 1,000 / 1.08¹⁰ = 1,000 / 2.158925 ≈ 463.19 million VND; also added to the asset's cost (Dr PP&E / Cr provision) and depreciated over its life.
Note: Each year the discount unwinds as an interest cost (AAC-053).

AAC-053.q: The increase in a provision due to the passage of time (unwinding of discount) is recognised as a finance cost.
AAC-053.x:
Basis: IAS 37, paragraph 60.
Analysis: True. A discounted provision grows as settlement nears (unwinding of discount) → the increase is a finance cost, not an operating expense. E.g., AAC-052: year 1 = 463.19 × 8% ≈ 37.06 million.

AAC-054.q: For an onerous contract, the provision is measured at:
AAC-054.e: Unavoidable costs are the least net cost of exiting the contract.
o: The lower of the net cost of fulfilling the contract and the penalty for exiting it
The full contract value
Lost expected profit
Allocated general overheads
AAC-054.x:
Basis: IAS 37, paragraphs 66–69.
Analysis: An onerous contract's unavoidable costs exceed expected benefits. The provision = the lower of net cost to fulfil (cost − benefit) and penalties or compensation for terminating – the entity would choose the cheapest exit (AAC-055).
Distractors: B, C and D aren't measurement bases.

AAC-055.q: A non-cancellable purchase commitment: cost to fulfil VND 1,200 million, economic benefits 1,000 million; exit penalty 300 million. What onerous contract provision is required (VND million)?
AAC-055.e: Net cost of fulfilling = 1,200 − 1,000 = 200 < penalty 300 → provision 200 million VND.
AAC-055.x:
Basis: IAS 37.
Working: Net cost to fulfil = 1,200 − 1,000 = 200 million; termination penalty = 300 million. Provision = min(200; 300) = 200 million VND.

AAC-056.q: A restructuring provision excludes costs of retraining continuing staff and marketing for future operations.
AAC-056.e: True. Only direct costs necessarily entailed by the restructuring, not associated with ongoing activities.
AAC-056.x:
Basis: VAS 18; IAS 37, paragraphs 80–81.
Analysis: True. Restructuring provisions include only direct costs necessarily caused by the restructuring and unrelated to continuing activities (severance, lease terminations). They exclude retraining remaining staff, marketing, new systems or distribution networks – future operating costs (IFR-151).

AAC-057.q: Select ALL disclosures required for accounting estimates with high uncertainty:
AAC-057.e: Users need assumptions and sensitivities to assess the risk of material adjustment.
o: Key assumptions
Sensitivity of carrying amounts to changes in assumptions
Nature of the related asset/liability
List of staff who prepared the estimate
AAC-057.x:
Basis: VAS 21; IAS 1/IFRS 18 (key sources of estimation uncertainty).
Analysis: Disclose: (A) key assumptions about the future; (B) sensitivity of carrying amounts to assumption changes and the range of reasonable outcomes; (C) the nature and carrying amount of affected assets and liabilities – so users can judge the risk of material adjustment next year.
Distractors: (D) Names of staff preparing estimates aren't useful to users.

AAC-058.q: Management bonus equals 10% of profit AFTER deducting the bonus itself. Profit before bonus is VND 2,000 million. What bonus must be accrued (VND million, 2 decimals)?
AAC-058.x:
Basis: VAS 01 (accruals); IAS 19 (short-term bonuses).
Working: B = 10% × (2,000 − B) → B = 200 − 0.1B → 1.1B = 200 → B = 181.82 million VND.
Check: profit after bonus = 2,000 − 181.82 = 1,818.18; × 10% = 181.82.

AAC-059.q: A specific loan of VND 1,000 million at 10% finances a factory build all year; temporarily idle funds earn interest of 20 million. What borrowing cost is capitalised (VND million)?
AAC-059.x:
Basis: VAS 16; IAS 23, paragraph 12.
Working: Specific borrowing: capitalised cost = actual interest 1,000 × 10% = 100 − income from temporarily investing idle funds 20 = 80 million VND.

AAC-060.q: An entity has two general loans: VND 2,000 million at 9% and 3,000 million at 11%. What is the weighted capitalisation rate (%)?
AAC-060.x:
Basis: VAS 16; IAS 23, paragraph 14 (capitalisation rate for general borrowings).
Working: Rate = total interest / total borrowings = (2,000 × 9% + 3,000 × 11%) / 5,000 = (180 + 330) / 5,000 = 510 / 5,000 = 10.2%.

AAC-061.q: An entity has two general loans: VND 2,000 million at 9% and 3,000 million at 11% (capitalisation rate 10.2%). Average accumulated expenditure on a qualifying asset is 1,500 million, funded by general borrowing. What borrowing cost is capitalised (VND million)?
AAC-061.e: 1,500 × 10.2% = 153 million VND (not exceeding actual interest incurred).
AAC-061.x:
Basis: VAS 16; IAS 23.
Working: Capitalised amount = average accumulated expenditure 1,500 × 10.2% = 153 million VND; checked against actual interest of 510 → 153 may be capitalised.

AAC-062.q: Capitalisation of borrowing costs must be suspended when:
AAC-062.e: Borrowing costs during abnormal interruptions are expensed.
o: Active development is interrupted for extended periods, unless the interruption is necessary
The entity changes lender
Interest rates rise
At the end of each quarter
AAC-062.x:
Basis: VAS 16; IAS 23, paragraphs 20–21.
Analysis: Capitalisation is suspended during extended interruptions (funding gaps, disputes), except necessary ones (concrete curing, regular local flood seasons); borrowing costs during abnormal interruptions are expensed.
Distractors: B, C and D aren't suspension triggers.

AAC-063.q: A building costing VND 10,000 million comprises roof and services of 1,000 million (10-year life) and the main structure of 9,000 million (45 years). What is annual component depreciation (straight-line) (VND million)?
AAC-063.x:
Basis: IAS 16 (component depreciation – IFR-107).
Working: Roof and services 1,000 / 10 = 100; main structure 9,000 / 45 = 200. Total = 300 million VND a year.
Note: A single 10,000 / 45 ≈ 222 million would understate cost.

AAC-064.q: A revalued asset has a carrying amount of VND 800 million with a prior revaluation surplus of 50 million; it is now revalued to 700 million. What loss goes to profit or loss (VND million)?
AAC-064.e: The decrease of 100 first reduces the 50 surplus (OCI); the remaining 50 goes to profit or loss.
AAC-064.x:
Basis: IAS 16, paragraph 40.
Working: Decrease = 800 − 700 = 100. First reduce the existing revaluation surplus by 50 (through OCI); the remaining 100 − 50 = 50 million VND goes to profit or loss.

AAC-065.q: A cash-generating unit has a carrying amount of VND 1,000 billion (including goodwill of 100 billion) and a recoverable amount of 850 billion. How much impairment is allocated to assets other than goodwill (VND billion)?
AAC-065.e: Loss 150: goodwill is written down by 100 first; the remaining 50 is allocated to other assets pro rata to carrying amounts.
AAC-065.x:
Basis: IAS 36, paragraph 104.
Working: Impairment = 1,000 − 850 = 150 billion. Allocation: goodwill first, 100; the remaining 50 billion to other CGU assets pro rata to carrying amounts (none below the highest of fair value less disposal costs, value in use and zero).

AAC-066.q: When reversing an impairment loss on an asset (other than goodwill), the carrying amount after reversal may not exceed what it would have been (net of depreciation) had no impairment been recognised.
AAC-066.x:
Basis: IAS 36, paragraph 117.
Analysis: True. Impairment reversals (when indicators or estimates change) are capped: the reversed carrying amount can't exceed what it would have been (net of depreciation) had no impairment been recognised – preventing disguised revaluation. Goodwill impairment is never reversed (IFR-113).

AAC-067.q: A 3-year warehouse lease with VND 200 million paid at the START of each year; incremental borrowing rate 8%. What is the present value of lease payments under IFRS 16, including the day-one payment (VND million, 2 decimals)?
AAC-067.e: 200 + 200/1.08 + 200/1.08² = 200 + 185.19 + 171.47 ≈ 556.65 million VND (the day-one payment forms part of the ROU asset).
AAC-067.x:
Basis: IFRS 16 (payments in advance).
Working: PV = 200 + 200/1.08 + 200/1.08² = 200 + 185.19 + 171.47 ≈ 556.65 million VND.
Note: Under IFRS 16 payments made at or before commencement aren't in the lease liability but added to the ROU asset; the liability after the day-one payment = 356.65. The question includes the day-one payment per its own wording.

AAC-068.q: A lease is modified to add another office floor at a price commensurate with its standalone price. Under IFRS 16:
AAC-068.e: Increased scope at a commensurate price → separate lease.
o: Account for it as a separate lease
Remeasure the whole original lease liability
Expense immediately
Do not recognise
AAC-068.x:
Basis: IFRS 16, paragraph 44.
Analysis: A lease modification is a separate lease when both: scope increases by adding the right to use more underlying assets (another floor); and consideration rises by the standalone (market) price of the addition. The original lease is unchanged.
Distractors: B applies to modifications failing those conditions; C and D are wrong.

AAC-069.q: Investment property under the fair value model rises from VND 5,000 to 5,400 million. What gain goes to profit or loss (VND million)?
AAC-069.e: 5,400 − 5,000 = 400 million VND; no depreciation is charged.
AAC-069.x:
Basis: IAS 40 (fair value model – IFR-119).
Working: Gain = 5,400 − 5,000 = 400 million VND, to profit or loss; no depreciation.

AAC-070.q: When owner-occupied property is transferred to investment property at fair value, an increase at the transfer date is treated as a revaluation under IAS 16 (in OCI).
AAC-070.x:
Basis: IAS 40, paragraphs 61–62; IAS 16.
Analysis: True. On transferring owner-occupied property (IAS 16) to investment property at fair value, the difference between carrying amount and fair value at transfer is treated as an IAS 16 revaluation – increases to OCI (except reversals of past losses), decreases to P&L. Later fair value changes go to P&L.

AAC-071.q: A VND 300 million government grant is received to buy a machine costing 1,200 million (10-year life); it is recorded as deferred income. How much is released to income each year (VND million)?
AAC-071.e: 300 / 10 = 30 million VND per year, matching depreciation.
AAC-071.x:
Basis: IAS 20 – Government grants.
Working: The 300 deferred income is released over the machine's life: 300 / 10 = 30 million VND a year – matching its 120 a year depreciation.
Note: IAS 20's alternative deducts the grant from cost (900) – depreciation 90 a year, with the same net profit effect.

AAC-072.q: An exchange of assets lacking commercial substance is measured at:
AAC-072.e: No gain or loss arises when the exchange lacks commercial substance.
o: The carrying amount of the asset given up
The fair value of the asset received
The higher market value
The contract value
AAC-072.x:
Basis: IAS 16, paragraphs 24–25 (asset exchanges).
Analysis: An exchange lacking commercial substance (no significant change in future cash flows) or without reliable fair values → the asset received is recorded at the carrying amount of the asset given; no gain or loss – preventing 'manufactured' profit by swapping similar assets.
Distractors: B applies to exchanges with commercial substance; C and D have no basis.

AAC-073.q: A USD 50,000 receivable was recorded at 24,800; the year-end rate is 25,300. What exchange gain arises on revaluation (VND million)?
AAC-073.x:
Basis: VAS 10; IAS 21.
Working: FX gain = 50,000 × (25,300 − 24,800) = 50,000 × 500 = 25,000,000 VND = 25 million VND (the receivable rises as USD strengthens).

AAC-074.q: Under Vietnamese accounting rules, when revaluing foreign-currency monetary items at period end:
AAC-074.e: This is the actual-rate principle for revaluation; IFRS uses the closing (spot) rate.
o: Monetary assets use the buying rate and liabilities the selling rate of the commercial bank the entity regularly uses
All items use the central rate
All items use the selling rate
No revaluation
AAC-074.x:
Basis: VAS 10; corporate accounting regime (Circulars 200/2014, 99/2025).
Analysis: Year-end revaluation uses actual rates: monetary assets (cash, receivables) at the buying rate; liabilities at the selling rate of the commercial bank the business regularly uses (ACC-068, ACC-103). IFRS uses one closing rate (IFR-143).
Distractors: B, C and D don't match the rules.

AAC-075.q: Foreign-currency advances to suppliers (to be settled in goods, not cash) are not revalued at period end.
AAC-075.x:
Basis: VAS 10; IAS 21 (ACC-079).
Analysis: True. Supplier prepayments settle in goods, not cash → non-monetary → kept at the transaction-date rate, not revalued at year-end.

AAC-076.q: A convertible bond is issued: face VND 1,000 million, 5% annual coupon in arrears, 3 years; market rate for similar non-convertible debt 8%. What is the equity component (VND million, 2 decimals)?
AAC-076.x:
Basis: IAS 32 (compound instruments – IFR-101).
Working: Liability = PV at 8%: 50/1.08 + 50/1.08² + 1,050/1.08³ = 46.30 + 42.87 + 833.52 ≈ 922.68. Equity component = 1,000 − 922.68 ≈ 77.32 million VND.
Note: Vietnamese accounting also separates the option element into account 4113.

AAC-077.q: An entity buys back its own shares (treasury shares) and later resells them above cost. The difference is recognised:
AAC-077.e: Transactions with owners in the entity's own shares are equity transactions.
o: In equity (share premium), not through profit or loss
In finance income
In other income
As a reduction of expenses
AAC-077.x:
Basis: IAS 32, paragraph 33; corporate accounting regime (accounts 419, 4112).
Analysis: Buying, selling, issuing or cancelling own shares are owner transactions → no gain or loss; the difference between resale and purchase price of treasury shares goes to equity (share premium).
Distractors: B, C and D route it through P&L – against the principle and open to profit manipulation.

AAC-078.q: 1 million shares of par VND 10,000 are issued at 25,000; issue costs VND 200 million. What share premium is recognised (VND million)?
AAC-078.e: 1,000,000 × (25,000 − 10,000) = 15,000 million; less issue costs of 200 → 14,800 million VND.
AAC-078.x:
Basis: Corporate accounting regime (accounts 4111, 4112); IAS 32.
Working: Share premium = 1,000,000 × (25,000 − 10,000) = 15,000 million; less issue costs 200 → 14,800 million VND. Contributed capital at par = 10,000 million.

AAC-079.q: A share dividend transfers part of retained earnings to contributed capital without changing total equity.
AAC-079.e: True. There is no cash outflow.
AAC-079.x:
Basis: Corporate accounting regime (FIN-041).
Analysis: True. A stock dividend: Dr 421 / Cr 4111 – an internal equity transfer, no cash outflow, total equity unchanged; share count rises and EPS is restated retrospectively (AAC-080).

AAC-080.q: Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders is VND 120 billion; 10 million shares outstanding all year; in October a 2-for-10 bonus issue is made. What is basic EPS (adjusted retrospectively for the bonus issue) (VND)?
AAC-080.e: Bonus shares are treated as outstanding from the start: 12 million; EPS = 120 billion / 12 million = 10,000 VND.
AAC-080.x:
Basis: VAS 30; IAS 33, paragraph 28 (bonus issues restated retrospectively).
Working: A 10:2 ratio → 10 million × 1.2 = 12 million shares, treated as outstanding all year (no time-weighting since no cash came in). EPS = 120 billion / 12 million = 10,000 VND (prior-year EPS is restated too).

AAC-081.q: A parent guarantees its subsidiary's bank loan for no fee. In the parent's separate IFRS 9 FS, the financial guarantee contract is:
AAC-081.e: Subsequently it is measured at the higher of the ECL allowance and the initial amount less amortisation.
o: Initially recognised at fair value (usually adding to the investment in the subsidiary)
Disclosed only
Recognised at the maximum guaranteed amount
Recognised when the subsidiary defaults
AAC-081.x:
Basis: IFRS 9 (financial guarantee contracts).
Analysis: In separate FS, a financial guarantee is initially recognised at fair value (the fee an independent party would charge); an unpaid guarantee for a subsidiary is usually offset by increasing the investment (an implicit capital contribution). Later it's measured at the higher of the ECL allowance and the initial amount less cumulative amortisation.
Distractors: B, C and D breach IFRS 9.

AAC-082.q: A bond is bought for VND 1,050 million (face 1,000, 10% coupon), at amortised cost with an effective rate of 8.5%. What is year-1 interest income (VND million)?
AAC-082.x:
Basis: IFRS 9 (amortised cost, effective interest – IFR-093).
Working: Year-1 interest income = 1,050 × 8.5% = 89.25 million. Coupon received = 1,000 × 10% = 100 → premium amortised = 100 − 89.25 = 10.75; year-end amortised cost = 1,050 − 10.75 = 1,039.25.

AAC-083.q: Under IFRS 9, trading securities are measured at fair value through profit or loss, including unrealised gains; under current Vietnamese rules a provision is mainly made when prices fall.
AAC-083.e: True. This is a key difference when converting from VAS to IFRS.
AAC-083.x:
Basis: IFRS 9; Circular 48/2019/TT-BTC (IFR-104).
Analysis: True. IFRS 9: trading securities at FVTPL, recognising unrealised gains and losses. Vietnam: at cost, with allowances only when market price falls below cost; gains only on sale. Conversion makes profit swing more with markets.

AAC-084.q: Select ALL monetary items (to be retranslated at period end):
AAC-084.e: Inventory and prepayments are non-monetary items.
o: USD bank deposits
EUR trade receivables
USD bank loans
Imported inventory
Office rent prepaid in USD
AAC-084.x:
Basis: VAS 10; IAS 21.
Analysis: Monetary items (received or paid in fixed amounts of money): (A) USD deposits; (B) EUR receivables; (C) USD loans → revalued at year-end.
Distractors: (D) imported inventory and (E) prepaid rent (settled by service) are non-monetary (AAC-075).

AAC-085.q: Arrange the year-end close at a multi-subsidiary group:
AAC-085.e: Consolidated figures are reliable only once each entity's separate FS are properly closed.
o: Fix cut-off and reconcile sub-ledgers to the general ledger
Accruals and amortisation of prepayments
Estimates: provisions, impairments, depreciation
FX revaluation, current and deferred tax
Reconcile intra-group balances and post consolidation entries
Management review and approval of the FS
AAC-085.x:
Basis: Closing practice; VAS 25.
Analysis: Order: cut-off and sub-ledger to GL reconciliation → accruals and prepayment amortisation → estimates for allowances, impairment, depreciation → FX revaluation, current and deferred tax (needing adjusted profit) → intercompany reconciliation and consolidation entries → management review and approval. Consolidation is only reliable once each entity's books are properly closed (ACC-109).

AAC-086.q: A VND 6,000 million loan at 9% per year is drawn on 01/10, with interest paid annually on 30/9. What interest must be accrued at 31/12 (VND million)?
AAC-086.x:
Basis: VAS 01 (accruals); VAS 16.
Working: Interest accrued from 01/10 to 31/12 = 6,000 × 9% × 3/12 = 135 million VND (Dr 635 / Cr 335 – ACC-058).

AAC-087.q: On 01/4 the entity pays VND 240 million for 12 months of property insurance. What prepaid balance remains at 31/12 (VND million)?
AAC-087.e: 9 months used (180); 3 months remain = 60 million VND.
AAC-087.x:
Basis: VAS 01 (matching principle).
Working: 240 for 12 months = 20 a month. From 01/04 to 31/12, 9 months used = 180 (expensed); 3 months = 60 million VND remain prepaid (account 242) at 31/12.

AAC-088.q: A material prior-year error is found this year. The correct treatment:
AAC-088.e: Material prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively under VAS 29/IAS 8.
o: Retrospective restatement: restate comparatives and adjust opening retained earnings
Take the full effect to this year's profit or loss
Ignore it because last year was audited
Disclose only
AAC-088.x:
Basis: VAS 29; IAS 8 (IFR-033).
Analysis: Material prior-period errors are corrected retrospectively: restate comparatives for the period of error, adjust opening retained earnings (and related items), and disclose nature and effects.
Distractors: B distorts this year's profit; C – a prior audit doesn't remove the duty; D isn't enough when material.

AAC-089.q: Last year's closing inventory was overstated by VND 100 million (material); tax rate 20%. By how much must this year's opening retained earnings be REDUCED (VND million)?
AAC-089.e: Last year's profit was overstated by 100, tax 20 → reduce by 100 × (1 − 20%) = 80 million VND.
AAC-089.x:
Basis: VAS 29; IAS 8.
Working: Prior year-end stock overstated by 100 → COGS understated, pre-tax profit overstated by 100, CIT overstated by 20 → after-tax profit inflated by 80 → reduce opening retained earnings by 80 million VND (inventory down 100, tax payable down / tax receivable 20).

AAC-090.q: An uncorrected overstatement of year-1 closing inventory understates year-2 profit by the same amount, so cumulative profit at the end of year 2 is correct (ignoring tax); each year's FS are still wrong.
AAC-090.e: True. It is a counterbalancing error; still corrected if material to comparatives.
AAC-090.x:
Basis: VAS 29.
Analysis: True. Overstated year-1 closing stock inflates year-1 profit; the same overstated year-2 opening stock raises year-2 COGS and cuts profit equally → cumulative profit at end of year 2 is right (a self-correcting error). But each year's statements (trends, EPS, annual tax) are still wrong; if material, comparatives must be restated.

AAC-091.q: Book bank balance VND 500 million; outstanding cheques 80; deposits in transit 50; unrecorded bank charges 2; bank interest credited but unrecorded 3 (VND million). What is the adjusted book balance (VND million)?
AAC-091.e: 500 − 2 + 3 = 501 million; outstanding cheques and deposits in transit adjust the bank side.
AAC-091.x:
Basis: Bank reconciliation practice (ICR-086, VSA-072).
Working: Book-side adjustments (items the bank recorded but the business hasn't): 500 − fees 2 + interest 3 = 501 million VND. Outstanding cheques (80) and deposits in transit (50) adjust the bank statement side (AAC-092).

AAC-092.q: Bank reconciliation: adjusted book balance (after bank charges and interest) is VND 501 million; outstanding cheques 80 million; deposits in transit 50 million. What must the bank statement balance be (VND million)?
AAC-092.e: Statement + deposits in transit − outstanding cheques = 501 → statement = 501 + 80 − 50 = 531 million VND.
AAC-092.x:
Basis: Bank reconciliation practice.
Working: Adjusted balance = statement + deposits in transit − outstanding cheques = 501 → statement = 501 − 50 + 80 = 531 million VND.
Note: If the statement differs from 531, the unexplained gap must be investigated (AAC-093).

AAC-093.q: At year-end an unexplained receivables/payables reconciliation difference of VND 120 million remains. The appropriate treatment:
AAC-093.e: 'Plugging' differences is a red flag for error and fraud.
o: Investigate and match documents; adjust only with evidence
Post it to other income to balance
Post it to admin expenses to balance
Leave it undisclosed
AAC-093.x:
Basis: Closing practice; VSA 240 (unusual adjusting entries).
Analysis: Unexplained balance differences must be investigated (wrong party, wrong period, missing invoices, disputes) and traced to documents; adjust only with support.
Distractors: B and C – 'plugging' to income or expense without basis is an error and fraud red flag; D ignores the problem.

AAC-094.q: Select ALL documents to review in year-end cut-off testing:
AAC-094.e: A decision effective next period is not a cut-off matter for this period.
o: Goods received notes/delivery records at year-end and early next year
Sales invoices and shipping documents around the closing date
Credit notes and returns early next year
Expense invoices for this year received next year
A pay-rise decision effective next year
AAC-094.x:
Basis: Closing practice; VSA 500.
Analysis: Cut-off documents to review: (A) goods-received notes around year-end and early next year – purchases in the right period; (B) sales invoices and shipping documents around the closing date – revenue cut-off (AAC-025); (C) credit notes and returns early next year – fictitious year-end sales (VSA-127); (D) this year's expense invoices received next year – accruals needed.
Distractors: (E) A decision effective next year doesn't affect this period.

AAC-095.q: Switching inventory costing from FIFO to weighted average to provide more relevant information is a change in accounting policy, applied retrospectively.
AAC-095.e: True (unless the retrospective effect is impracticable to determine).
AAC-095.x:
Basis: VAS 29; IAS 8 (IFR-031).
Analysis: True. The inventory cost formula is an accounting policy; voluntarily switching from FIFO to weighted average for more reliable, relevant information → a policy change, applied retrospectively (adjusting opening balances – AAC-096) unless the effect can't be determined.
Note: For tax, the method must be applied consistently within the year and notified.

AAC-096.q: A new accounting policy increases opening inventory by VND 50 million; tax rate 20%. By how much do opening retained earnings increase (VND million)?
AAC-096.x:
Basis: VAS 29; IAS 8.
Working: Opening stock up 50 → cumulative prior pre-tax profit up 50, with 10 of related tax → opening retained earnings up 50 × (1 − 20%) = 40 million VND.

AAC-097.q: When comparatives are reclassified (e.g., moving an expense from admin to selling), the entity must:
o: Disclose the nature, amount and reason for the reclassification
Disclose nothing
Adjust last year's profit
Seek tax authority approval
AAC-097.x:
Basis: VAS 21; IFRS 18 (reclassifying comparatives).
Analysis: When presentation or classification changes, comparatives are reclassified with disclosure of nature, amounts and reasons – preserving comparability. Reclassification doesn't change profit.
Distractors: B lacks disclosure; C – profit doesn't change; D – no tax approval is needed.

AAC-098.q: In February next year (before the FS are issued), a customer owing VND 300 million at 31/12 goes bankrupt; 20% is expected to be recovered. No provision exists. What additional provision is recognised in this year's FS (VND million)?
AAC-098.e: An adjusting event (evidence of conditions at 31/12): 300 × 80% = 240 million VND.
AAC-098.x:
Basis: VAS 23; IAS 10 (ACC-034, IFR-034).
Working: A February bankruptcy evidences the receivable was impaired at 31/12 (the customer was usually already struggling) → an adjusting event. Allowance = 300 × (1 − 20%) = 240 million VND, booked in this year's FS.

AAC-099.q: If events after the reporting period show the going concern assumption is no longer appropriate, the entity must reconsider the basis of preparation even though the event occurred after period end.
AAC-099.e: True under VAS 23/IAS 10: FS are not prepared on a going concern basis if management intends to liquidate or has no realistic alternative.
AAC-099.x:
Basis: VAS 23; IAS 10, paragraphs 14–16 (IFR-036).
Analysis: True. A key exception to non-adjusting events: if after the period end management intends to liquidate or cease trading, or has no realistic alternative, the FS can't be prepared on a going-concern basis – changing the whole basis, not just disclosure.

AAC-100.q: Consider these statements on closing practice:
AAC-100.e: Revenue follows transfer of control; unsupported manual entries are a fraud red flag.
o: Costs incurred but not yet invoiced must be accrued.
Revenue is recognised on invoicing regardless of delivery.
Intra-group balances are reconciled before consolidation eliminations.
Unsupported round-sum manual adjustments may be posted to balance figures.
AAC-100.x:
Basis: VAS 01; VAS 14; VSA 240.
Analysis: True: accrue costs incurred but not yet invoiced (accruals); reconcile intercompany balances before consolidation eliminations (AAC-085). False: revenue follows transfer of control, not invoicing (AAC-024); round-number manual entries without support are fraud red flags (VSA-053) – never used to 'force' balances.
